source.source_title: LeakageBench: Document-Level Leakage Risk for Redacting Personally Identifiable Information in Document Images
source.primary_analysis_display_assumption: Nearest 0.001, inclusive half-unit endpoints; both tie conventions admitted
source.applicability_assumption: Common full-schema Direct+Linkage applicable-page set for all Table 3 systems
source.validity_assumption: The reported page-validity indicator is the page-level unusable-output predicate; its false outcomes are scored as empty prediction sets
source.source_limitations: Challenge-set page counts and typed IoU matching; no deployment sampling claim, no final-artifact containment measurement
source.redistribution: Only numerical facts, system labels, original code and analysis are included. Full paper HTML is not redistributed.

primary_source_locators.paraphrase: Headline DocLeak uses same-type matching at an IoU threshold; it is not complete-mask containment.
Each DocLeak denominator consists of pages containing an in-scope gold identifier.
Full-schema evaluation retains unsupported labels as misses. Page validity describes parseable, schema-conformant output; malformed or unusable outputs are scored as empty predictions.
The separate supported-type evaluation changes the gold scope by system and is excluded from this reconstruction.
The corpus has 500 pages from 291 source documents.

primary_source_locators.locator: Appendix B, OCR-free conversion and validation
primary_source_locators.paraphrase: The invalid-output conversion is described before scoring, without model-specific repair.
